doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Scoring Dan August for Quinn Martin with Hollywood's best players
summary: Grusin recommended him for Dan August; Scott conducted a top orchestra and recalls the elation.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah, “The Fugitive,” “Cannon,” “Streets of San Francisco,” “Barnaby Jones,” and more. But this was a show in 1969 I believe starring a then-unknown actor named Burt Reynolds. And it was called “Dan August.” And Dave had written a great theme for this show, wonderful, wonderful theme. But he was doing feature films by that time so he couldn’t do the weekly underscore for the show. So he told that music supervisor, another wonderful guy named John Elizalde, music supervisor for Quinn Martin Productions but

also a damn good composer in his own right. But anyway Dave said why don’t you get Tom, and so I was hired to do an episode of “Dan August” which I still remember the joy, the elation of standing on a podium with all the best musicians in Hollywood, you know I had Vince DeRosa on French horn, I think Ray Brown played bass, you know Bud Shank on woodwinds and just you know, and the best violin players in the business. Erno Neufeld I think was the great, great concertmaster at that time. And it was just, oh my gosh I can’t tell you how good it felt to just hear this music coming back at you. It was a delight. I’ll never forget it. So that’s how it started.
